articles.title: Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey Comes to Digital With Over 90 Minutes of Bonus Features
articles.summary: Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey has landed on digital platforms. The move to digital comes exactly four months after the movie’s initial release in theaters, making it the longest theatrical window of 2026. Why would you rush the digital release for a movie that keeps selling out?
body: If you somehow didn’t catch the movie in theaters, or are already itching for the at-home rewatch, here’s where to find the movie on digital as well as all of the info we have about The Odyssey’s streaming and home entertainment releases.

The Odyssey is now available to rent or purchase digitally ( see at Prime Video ). Choosing to purchase the movie will net you over 90 minutes of bonus features across 12 behind-the-scenes featurettes.

The Odyssey, which boasts a full runtime of almost three hours, is legendary director Christopher Nolan’s take on Ulysses’ epic. Matt Damon stars as Odysseus, while future Bond himself, Robert Pattinson, goes full weasel mode in the role of Antinous.

This is Nolan we’re talking about, so the movie can be aptly described as a full spectacle. The man is very dedicated to his special effects, which are in full display across The Odyssey’s mythology-inspired sequences.

articles.title: There Really Is No Escape From The Duolingo Owl, Who Will Soon Join Pokémon Go
articles.summary: Not content with plaguing your phone's lock screen, Duo the Duolingo owl is next set to appear in Pokémon Go. A crossover between the two hugely-popular smartphone apps has been announced, unlocking bonuses for players in both experiences.
body: The fun begins on November 17, when a time-limited event begins in Duolingo that requires you to complete at least one language lesson on seven separate days. This will then unlock a series of Pokémon-themed outfits for your Duolingo profile.

Completing all of that will also grant a promo code for Pokémon Go, unlocking timed research that awards Pokémon such as Pikachu and regional exclusive Chatot with a unique Duolingo background. It's rather cute — even if it does feature more of Duo the owl, too.

Why is all of this happening? While Pokémon Go has featured sponsored cosmetic items in the past, the game rarely offers this level of collaboration, and particularly not with another smartphone app. Still, earlier this year, the game also partnered with LEGO to offer similar bonus gameplay, centered around LEGO stores.

articles.title: 30 Years Later, One of the Greatest ‘X-Files’ Episodes is Still a Misunderstood Masterpiece
articles.summary: For the first three seasons of The X-Files, the writers kept you guessing, not only with regard to the show’s greater mysteries about aliens, but also about its most intriguing character. The Cigarette Smoking Man, played by William B.
body: We’re led to assume that he’s some high-ranking G-man who’s privy to the government’s darkest secrets — and nothing else. We never get a definitive name or clarity about his position. His sporadic appearances always leave the viewers wanting to know more, but in season 4, the show finally provides perhaps too much information, while still managing to create a classic, memorable episode.

Debuting on Nov. 17, 1996, “Musings of a Cigarette Smoking Man” was the seventh episode of The X-Files' fourth season. It begins with a rather shocking setup, which shows the Cigarette Smoking Man pointing a rifle out of the window of a building. In his crosshairs is Melvin Frohike (Tom Braidwood), part of the trio of conspiracy theorists who run a tabloid called The Lone Gunmen. The Cigarette Smoking Man listens in on Frohike’s conversation with Mulder and Scully as he prepares to fire.

Frohike tells Mulder and Scully that he may have discovered the history of the Cigarette Smoking Man, and he begins by talking about the most notorious conspiracy in American history: the assassination of President John F. Kennedy.

articles.title: The "Next James Bond" Actors Who Never Played James Bond
articles.summary: While there have only been seven actors to have been officially cast as 007, there have been dozens the media has erroneously labeled as “the next James Bond.”
body: It's been five years since No Time to Die, Daniel Craig's final James Bond film, was released and we finally officially know for certain who his successor is for the role of 007: Robert Pattinson.

Even before Craig stepped down, the rumor mill was in overdrive speculating about who would succeed him in the role of 007. This has been a media tradition throughout the franchise’s long history ever since Sean Connery retired his license to kill. But while there have only been now seven actors to (officially) play 007 onscreen, there have been dozens that the media has erroneously labeled as being “the next James Bond.”

For the purposes of this feature not running longer than SPECTRE, we’re going to just narrow it down to those actors most often reported as “the next James Bond” in the Daniel Craig era, starting from the time Pierce Brosnan exited the franchise in 2002 until the present.
Here then are all the actors who had been pegged as the Next James Bond … and who never ended up playing Bond (well, not yet anyway).

articles.title: The Head Of GTA 6’s Parent Company Helped Make One Of The Best Christmas Movies Of All Time
articles.summary: One of the most memorable and beloved Christmas movies is 1990's Home Alone, but it almost didn't happen, and the head of GTA 6 's parent company played a role in bringing the movie to market.
body: Strauss Zelnick, the current CEO of Rockstar Games owner Take-Two, was the president and COO of 20th Century Fox at the time--he was among the youngest-ever Hollywood CEOs at the age of 32.

Warner Bros. was originally backing Home Alone and had actually begun production on the movie until budget concerns prompted the studio to pull the plug. "Four days into production, they shut down the picture and canceled it. That never happens," Zelnick told David Rubenstein.

Fox, under the leadership of chairman Joe Roth and Zelnick as president, swooped in and gave the filmmakers--including director Christopher Columbus and writer John Hughes--the money to make Home Alone.

That turned out to be a fantastic investment for Fox, as Home Alone ranked as one of the top five highest-grossing movies of the year in the US. It grossed more than $476 million globally against a $13 million budget, and it picked up two Oscar nominations. Home Alone also helped launch the career of Macaulay Culkin, and his role of Kevin remains his most memorable part.

articles.title: How 2026's Best Video Games Were Made
articles.summary: Ahead of The Game Awards Game of the Year nominees, creatives behind Resident Evil, Control, Star Wars, and Pragmata pull back the curtain
body: What is great "game direction"? We love asking those in charge because everyone's answer is different.

Players' minds tend to jump to cinematic AAA blockbusters, where cutscenes and spectacle make the director's hand easy to recognize. But the beauty of video games is that greatness comes in endless forms. To prove out the point, Polygon assembled some of the creative minds behind 2026's most ambitious games to dig into what we believe remains a misunderstood art: the delicate balance of artistic vision, technical execution, and player experience that can transform a collection of ideas into a Game of the Year contender.
These wildly different philosophies all arrive at the same challenge: How do you make something that feels unmistakably your own while remembering that somebody actually has to enjoy playing it?

articles.title: WoW: Forever’s Dungeons Have Gotten Yet Another Big Change
articles.summary: World of Warcraft: Forever's dungeons have changed once again, with developer Blizzard's most recent adjustment requiring an emergency hotfix to address players' outcry.
body: Dungeons, specifically how much experience points players earn from them, have been one of Forever's most debated topics going back to the game's beta. Make them too lucrative, and players will just stay inside dungeons instead of questing out in the world. At the same time, Blizzard doesn't want dungeons to be one-time affairs, with players completing all their quests in a single run and never going back.

Blizzard opened a new front in the dungeon wars on November 13, making a change so that nobody in a dungeon group would receive any experience if enemies were considered "trivial" to to any player in the group. The idea behind this appeared to be an effort to prevent high-level players from running low-level ones through dungeons, in the process curtailing players from selling character "boosting" services to lowbies.

articles.title: GTA 6 Should Help Boost PS5 And Xbox Sales, But Their Astronomical Prices Could Hurt
articles.summary: Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 launches on November 19, and it's expected to help boost console sales for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. But the uptick in hardware sales might not be as dramatic as you might think--and there is a good reason why.
body: According to Circana's Mat Piscatella, there will be "probably" be a boost to PS5 and Xbox Series X|S sales when GTA 6 comes out, but the uptick could be muted due to the recent PS5 and Xbox Series X|S price hikes. Piscatella said anyone who is excited for GTA 6 and needs a new console might think twice when they see how astronomically expensive new consoles have become today.

When GTA 5 launched in 2013, the average price paid for a new PS3 was $252 and the Xbox 360 was $232. Adjusted for inflation, that would be $363 for the PS3 today and $334 for the Xbox 360. Those prices are significantly below the average price of a new PS5 ($646) and Xbox Series X|S ($663) today.

Earlier this year, Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick, who oversees the company launching GTA 6, said, "The rising cost of hardware is not a good thing." At the same time, Zelnick isn't worried about the impact on GTA 6, in part because he believes the game is so good that people will find a way to pay for a new console.

articles.title: Original GTA 6 leaker pleads guilty to hacking Rockstar Games, years after first revealing Lucia
articles.summary: The 21-year-old responsible for hacking Rockstar Games and leaking in-development GTA 6 footage in 2022 has pleaded guilty to a number of offenses.
body: The GTA 6 leaker was initially sentenced to an indefinite stay at a hospital due to his severe autism, but was more recently deemed fit for trial and moved to a regular prison earlier this January. On Monday, at the Woolwich Crown Court in South East London, he pleaded guilty to hacking Rockstar Games and a number of other companies, including Uber and EE/BT, in cyber attacks estimated to have caused £10m in damages.

At the time of his Rockstar hack - when he was between the ages of 16 and 17 - the leaker was already under police protection at a Travelodge hotel to keep him from rival hackers he had allegedly stolen Bitcoin from. Somewhat surprisingly, he then managed to hack the multi-billion dollar game maker with nothing but an Amazon Fire Stick, the hotel room's TV and a bluetooth-connected keyboard and mouse.

As the BBC reports, he also managed to break into the developer's Slack channels, before threatening to release the GTA 6 source code if Rockstar failed to contact him within the day. The leaker has yet to be sentenced.

articles.title: That 007 First Light theme song I didn't like is up for a Grammy Award
articles.summary: Remember that 007 First Light song Lana Del Rey surprised-dropped earlier this year that I said wasn't very good because, as I put it at the time, "it sounds like Bond karaoke"? Well anyway, it's up for a Grammy Award.
body: I haven't heard any of the other tracks in contention (in my defense, neither Ghost of Yotei nor Wolverine are available on PC, and I actively dislike Star Wars) but after listening to the 007 First Light theme again, and with more time to think about it, I will say this: My initial assessment was absolutely correct.

This is not a good Bond theme. Lana Del Rey may be tremendously talented, but that's lost in the all-consuming effort to hit all the notes without understanding what connects them: The end result is a pale imitation built out of a musical stereotype that's readily identifiable as someone trying really hard to do a Bond theme based on what they were told a Bond theme is supposed to sound like.

The Grammy Awards are a music industry award, not a game award, and that means some games that you might expect to be nominated are sometimes excluded: The rules for the videogame category state that "videogames that contain music but are not available as stand-alone audio streams/releases" are not eligible for consideration, for example. So if you don't see your favorite of the year in the list, that might be why.
